title: Radix Primitives
tagline: Unstyled, accessible React primitives with correct keyboard behavior built in.
note: The default answer for dialogs, menus, and popovers. Steal the composition API — parts, not props — and never hand-roll focus trapping again.

title: React Aria
tagline: Adobe's behavior hooks with the deepest accessibility thinking in open source.
note: Separates behavior from styling completely — hooks for logic, your CSS for looks. When Radix can't cover a complex widget, this is the next level down.

title: Headless UI
tagline: The Tailwind team's unstyled components, with a gentle transitions API.
note: If you live in Tailwind, start here. The enter/leave transition model is the kindest way to add motion to menus and dialogs without reaching for a library.

title: Base UI
tagline: The Radix lineage continued: accessible primitives with modern form controls.
note: Watch how it handles the hard parts other libraries dodge — sliders, selects, composite widgets. The direction Radix's thinking is heading.

title: shadcn/ui
tagline: Copy-paste components you own, distributed through a registry model.
note: The innovation isn't the components — it's distribution without dependency. Steal the registry idea for your own system: versioned, installable, forkable by default.

title: Lucide
tagline: The community Feather fork that won: consistent stroke icons for every framework.
note: Default icon set for new projects. Consistent 24px grid, tree-shakeable, every framework covered — the boring choice that ends icon debates.

title: Heroicons
tagline: Hand-crafted Tailwind icons in outline and solid — a lesson in optical sizing.
note: Small set, impeccable craft. Compare outline vs solid at 16px to learn why icons need grades, then decide if you need a bigger library at all.

title: Phosphor Icons
tagline: Six weights per icon — the fastest way to learn why icons need grades.
note: Thin for marketing pages, bold for dense UI, duotone for flair — one family, six voices. The weight axis alone justifies switching from a flat set.

title: Motion
tagline: Framer Motion's successor: spring physics with sensible defaults, any framework.
note: Springs over durations for anything that moves with intent. The layout-animation API remains the fastest path from static mock to living interface.

title: React Spring
tagline: Physics-based animation with trails and chains for orchestrated lists.
note: When Motion's springs aren't enough control, come here. useTrail and useChain are the vocabulary for staggered, choreographed UI that still feels physical.

title: Google Fonts
tagline: Open-licensed fonts with variable axes — filter by axis, not just family.
note: The variable-font filter is the feature: weight, width, and optical-size axes in one file. Prototype type systems here before committing to a paid family.

title: Fontsource
tagline: Self-host any open font via npm and kill the render-blocking font request.
note: One install, subsetted weights, zero third-party requests. The performance argument for self-hosting ends here — pair with next/font and move on.

title: MDN Web Docs
tagline: The canonical web reference — the compatibility tables are the product.
note: Folded into Libraries as a reference, per the IA decision. When an agent or teammate asserts browser support, this is the only citation that counts.

title: Can I Use
tagline: One lookup before every modern CSS decision.
note: Check here before reaching for a polyfill or a fallback. Pair it with Baseline guidance and most 'is it safe yet' debates resolve in seconds.

title: easings.net
tagline: Every easing visualized, with cubic-bezier values ready to copy.
note: Default to easeOutExpo for UI entrances and stop using ease-in-out for everything. One page that permanently upgrades your motion taste.
